title: Technical exercise library and hire evaluation guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a canonical exercise library + evaluation guidance for practical hiring assessments across engineering, data, and product roles. It intends to reduce bias, speed interviewer calibration, and create clearer handoffs into onboarding by tying observed signals to first-week ramp tasks.

Scope and principles:
- Use role-family templates (backend, infra, frontend, ml infra, model infra, applied-ml, product-analytics) rather than ad-hoc problems.
- Prefer timeboxed, implementable exercises (30–120 minutes for take-homes; 20–45 minutes for live coding) with clear evaluation criteria.
- Surface collaboration and communication expectations as part of the score (not only raw correctness).
- Maintain a small canonical set per role family — changes must be approved by people-ops + hiring manager.

How to pick an exercise for a role opening:
1) Identify role family and seniority band (IC2/IC3/Staff/etc.).
2) Choose one short live exercise and one optional take-home from the same family.
3) Confirm with hiring manager: does the exercise map to day-30 job tasks? If not, adjust.
4) Add the chosen exercise to the candidate packet and calendar invite; include test data and success criteria.

Exercise catalog (examples and intent):
- Backend: "API pagination + idempotency" (45m live): small REST endpoint + data model, include error handling and idempotent retry behavior. Tests included. Focus: system design tradeoffs at small scale, testability.
- Infra/SRE: "Incident triage simulation" (60m live + 30m writeup): simulated alert stream, ask candidate to triage and propose immediate mitigations and a postmortem outline. Focus: prioritization under ambiguity, runbook thinking.
- Frontend: "Accessible widget rebuild" (60m take-home): recreate a small interactive component with keyboard accessibility and responsive behavior. Focus: UX judgement and DOM APIs.
- Applied ML: "Data drift detection mini-kit" (2h take-home): provide a dataset snapshot and a scoring notebook; ask candidate to detect and explain drift and propose a monitoring signal. Focus: statistical reasoning + practical monitoring design.
- Data/Product analytics: "Funnel stratification" (45m take-home): given event logs, ask candidate to compute key metrics, identify segments with regressions, propose hypotheses. Focus: SQL + critical thinking.

Standardized rubric (single-sheet scoring to attach to interview feedback):
- Correctness / solution viability  (0-5)  weight 40%
- Design & tradeoffs             (0-4)  weight 25%
- Code quality / reproducibility  (0-4)  weight 15%
- Communication & explanation    (0-3)  weight 10%
- Culture / ownership signals     (0-2)  weight 10%
Scoring notes: provide explicit examples for each score level in the exercise template. Example: Correctness 5 = passes all provided tests and handles error edge cases; 3 = passes main cases but misses edge conditions; 0 = no meaningful attempt.

Pass thresholds and interview flow tie-ins:
- Passing composite score: >= 70% from the exercise segment alone for senior ICs; >= 60% for junior roles.
- For borderline candidates (60–75%) require calibration: at least two interviewers must annotate where they saw potential gaps and suggest paired ramp tasks.
- If an exercise reveals weakness in a non-critical skill but excellent potential, the hiring manager can authorize a conditional offer with a 30-day competency check tied to onboarding tasks.

Calibration sessions and maintenence:
- Monthly 30–45m calibration clinics per function: people-ops coordinates with hiring managers to review 3 anonymized exercise evaluations and realign on score mapping.
- Change control: update exercise templates only with a PR to /confluence/hiring-exercises and two approvers (people-ops + hiring manager).

Bias mitigation checklist (required for each exercise):
- Keep prompts domain-neutral; avoid company-specific trivia.
- Allow candidates to use familiar tools and languages; focus prompts on concepts not syntax.
- Provide starter scaffolding for take-homes so candidates can demonstrate reasoning even if time-limited.

Onboarding handoffs (how exercise signals map to first-week tasks):
- For each exercise template include a "handoff card": 3 observable strengths from the exercise and corresponding first-week concrete tasks. Examples:
  - Strength: "writes concise, testable endpoints" -> Week 1 task: ship a small API bugfix with accompanying unit tests and CI gate.
  - Strength: "clear incident prioritization" -> Week 1 task: shadow on-call triage and contribute a 1-page runbook update.
  - Weakness: "lack of infra tracing knowledge" -> Week 1 task: guided pairing to instrument one service call and a short quiz.
- Use these handoff cards in the offer packet and new-hire kickoff so managers can prioritize early mentoring.

Contract-to-perm conversion guidance (intersection with exercises):
- When evaluating contractors for perm conversion, use a short conversion exercise (30–60m) that maps to the contractor's existing deliverables.
- Conversion criteria: stable output quality over last 90 days + exercise composite >= 65% + manager recommendation.
- If conversion is recommended but exercise scores are marginal, consider a 60-day "conversion ramp" with milestone-based acceptance criteria.

Operational notes and templates to attach to candidate packet (links below):
- Candidate packet template (includes tests, env setup, acceptance criteria).
- Interviewer scoring sheet (single page) with explicit language for each band.
- Email templates: scheduling, take-home instructions, feedback turnaround expectation (target 5 business days).

Open questions and next steps (owners):
- [Sofia] Draft 6 canonical exercises for applied-ml family by 2025-11-20.
- [People-ops] Schedule first cross-function calibration 2025-11-28.
- [Hiring managers] Provide 3 real job-to-exercise mappings for current openings by 2025-11-14.

Appendix: quick-start checklist for interviewers
- Read exercise template + scoring examples before call.
- Print the rubric and mark notes live.
- Avoid leading language; ask candidate to explain tradeoffs.
- Submit feedback within 48 hours with explicit pass/fail recommendation and one concrete example observed.

Document history: draft v0.1 2025-11-02 initial outline; v0.2 2025-11-10 added onboarding handoff cards and conversion rules.
